title: What qualifications do you need for a plumbing or gasfitting licence in NSW?
description: NSW plumbing, draining and gasfitting licence types, the Certificate III and IV qualifications, 2 year experience rule, terms, police checks and CPD status.
shortAnswer: In New South Wales, Building Commission NSW issues plumbing, draining and gasfitting licences as contractor licences, qualified supervisor certificates and tradesperson certificates. A tradesperson certificate needs Certificate III in Plumbing (CPC32420 or later); a contractor licence or supervisor certificate for plumbing, draining and gasfitting needs Certificate IV in Plumbing and Services (CPC40920 or later) plus two years' industry experience. Licences run for 1, 3 or 5 years.
keyTakeaways: There are four licence types: individual contractor licence, company or partnership contractor licence, qualified supervisor certificate, and tradesperson or provisional tradesperson certificate.

Contractor licences and supervisor certificates for full plumbing, draining and gasfitting require Certificate IV in Plumbing and Services (Operations) and at least two years' combined industry experience, counted from completion of an apprenticeship or from the Certificate III date.
Current qualification requirements apply to qualifications completed from November 1, 2024. Qualifications finished in full before that date can be used under a transitional arrangement.
Every individual applicant must provide a National Police Check no older than 4 months, and apprentices or trainees cannot be issued a licence.
Building Commission NSW publishes CPD rules for builders, pool builders, certifiers and practitioners; its CPD page does not list plumbing, draining or gasfitting licences.
regulator: Building Commission NSW, administering licensing under the Home Building Act 1989 (NSW) and the Home Building Regulation 2014 (NSW); gasfitting work is defined by the Gas Supply Act 1996 (NSW)
appliesTo: Plumbers, drainers and gasfitters seeking or renewing a NSW licence or certificate
Businesses contracting for plumbing, draining or gasfitting work in NSW
LP gas, fire protection, fire sprinkler and urban irrigation specialists
Apprentices completing training and RTOs delivering CPC qualifications

sections.heading: Who licenses plumbers and gasfitters in NSW?

blocks.text: Plumbing, draining and gasfitting licences in New South Wales are administered by Building Commission NSW, and applications are lodged through Service NSW. The [NSW Government licensing page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/licences-and-credentials/building-and-trade-licences-and-registrations/plumbing-draining-and-gasfitting) says the categories of work are described in Schedule 4 of the Home Building Regulation 2014, and that gasfitting work is defined by the Gas Supply Act 1996.

Older guidance and many training resources still refer to NSW Fair Trading as the licensing body. The pages cited here are managed by Building Commission NSW, which should be named in current policies and contractor prequalification documents.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects Building Commission NSW guidance as at November 2026. The underlying qualification instrument, the Order on qualifications and experience for plumbing, gasfitting and related specialist work, sets the transitional list; check it before relying on an older qualification.

sections.heading: Which licence or certificate do I need?

blocks.text: The licence depends on the role: contracting for the work, supervising it, doing it, or a combination. Each can be issued for 1, 3 or 5 years, except the provisional tradesperson certificate, which is issued for 3 years and cannot be renewed.

blocks.text: Building Commission NSW publishes the company and partnership requirements on a separate page, so they are not summarized here. Specialist categories carry their own qualifications, set out below.

sections.heading: What are the qualifications for gasfitting, LP gas and other specialist categories?

blocks.text: For a contractor licence or supervisor certificate in gasfitting and restricted LP gasfitting, the applicant needs Certificate III in Plumbing (CPC32420 or later) or Certificate III in Gas Fitting (CPC32720 or later), plus listed units including accessing and interpreting regulatory requirements for the plumbing and services industry and designing and sizing consumer gas installations. Two years' combined industry experience is also required.

items: Restricted LP gasfitting covers LPG installations in vapour phase only at pressures not exceeding 150 kilopascals. Advanced LP gasfitting has no pressure or phase restriction and includes LPG transport container work.
Water plumbing for fire protection systems or fire sprinkler systems can be based on Certificate III in Plumbing or Certificate III in Fire Protection (CPC32820 or later), each with additional units.
Urban irrigation can be based on Certificate III in Plumbing or Certificate III in Irrigation Technology (AHC32419 or later), with irrigation and backflow prevention units.
Draining work can be based on Certificate III in Plumbing or Certificate II in Drainage (CPC20720 or later), with drainage design units for contractor and supervisor applications.

A tradesperson certificate in gasfitting can be based on Certificate III in Plumbing (CPC32420 or later), an earlier Certificate III with all gas services stream units, or Certificate III in Gasfitting.

sections.heading: How is the two years' experience counted?

blocks.text: Experience means work as an employee paid under an award or enterprise agreement. It can be gained during or after an apprenticeship or traineeship. Without a completed apprenticeship, experience only counts from the date the Certificate III in Plumbing (or other relevant qualification) was issued, and anything earlier is not accepted. Referees verify the experience on the Referee Statement for plumbing categories.

Proof of an apprenticeship is usually a NSW Certificate of Proficiency. Building Commission NSW distinguishes two types: a TCID certificate, showing a Training Contract ID and accepted as proof of an apprenticeship, and a TSR certificate issued through Trade Skills Recognition, which is not accepted where apprenticeship evidence is required. A person who previously held an unrestricted plumbing, draining and gasfitting contractor licence, supervisor certificate or tradesperson certificate need not show qualifications again.

sections.heading: Do NSW plumbers and gasfitters have to do CPD?

blocks.text: Not on current Building Commission NSW guidance. Its [CPD page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/licences-and-credentials/building-and-trade-licences-and-registrations/continuing-professional-development) sets requirements for residential and swimming pool builders, certifiers, design and building practitioners and professional engineers, and plumbing, draining and gasfitting licences are not on that list.

The renewal process is administrative. The [renewal page](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/licences-and-credentials/building-and-trade-licences-and-registrations/renew-restore-or-replace) states that an unrenewed licence expires and the holder is no longer authorized to work, that a licence can be restored if it expired less than 3 months ago, and that after that a new application may be needed. Renewal cannot be done online where the holder has matters to declare, such as criminal charges, insolvency or compliance issues.

Because there is no mandated refresher, ongoing competence on gas safety and changes to AS/NZS 3500 or gas installation standards falls to the employer's general training duty. Compare Victoria's mandatory scheme for electricians on the [electrical licence CPD page](/regulations/australian-electrical-licence-cpd).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each licence category as a credential with the qualification and units that underpin it, so a gap such as a missing consumer gas design unit is visible before a supervisor application. Where no CPD is mandated, the same framework holds the employer's own refresher topics against the standards they cover. See how this applies to [energy and resources organizations](/industries/energy-resources).

faqs.q: Can an apprentice plumber hold a NSW licence?
faqs.a: No. Building Commission NSW states that a current apprentice or trainee cannot be issued a licence or certificate. After completing the apprenticeship, the person applies for the relevant licence, and the experience gained during the apprenticeship can count toward the two years needed for a contractor licence or supervisor certificate.

faqs.q: Does a NSW plumbing licence work interstate?
faqs.a: Plumbing, draining and gasfitting is included in the NSW Automatic Mutual Recognition scheme. Interstate and New Zealand licence holders wanting to work in NSW should follow the working interstate and mutual recognition guidance before starting work.

faqs.q: What if my qualification was completed before November 1, 2024?
faqs.a: Building Commission NSW will accept an applicable qualification and units completed in full before November 1, 2024 in place of the current requirements. Applicants cannot mix transitional and current requirements, and need a certificate or final academic transcript proving completion before that date.

faqs.q: Is a police check required to renew a plumbing licence?
faqs.a: Building Commission NSW requires a National Police Check no older than 4 months for all individual applications. Renewal holders who have new matters to declare, such as criminal charges, cannot renew online and must renew at a Service NSW center.

Contractor licence or supervisor certificate for plumbing, draining, gasfitting and LP gasfitting requires CPC40920 Certificate IV in Plumbing and Services (Operations) and at least two years' combined industry experience

Tradesperson certificate requires Certificate III in Plumbing CPC32420 or later; gasfitting contractor requires Cert III Plumbing or Cert III Gas Fitting CPC32720 plus units including design and size consumer gas installations
Restricted LP gasfitting: LPG vapour phase not exceeding 150 kPa; categories described in Schedule 4 of Home Building Regulation 2014; gasfitting defined by Gas Supply Act 1996

Transitional arrangement for qualifications completed before 1 November 2024; TCID CoP accepted, TSR CoP not accepted as apprenticeship evidence; apprentices cannot be issued a licence; experience counts from Cert III date if no apprenticeship
